title.narrative: Strengthened capacity of member States to ratify and apply international labour standards and to fulfil their reporting obligations

description.narrative:
Kenya’s 2010 Constitution reaffirmed the country’s commitment to international obligations, including ratifying and applying International Labour Organization (ILO) Conventions. However, challenges persist in the interpretation, implementation, and enforcement of these conventions in line with national laws and practice. Gaps in application have contributed to ongoing labour violations, including child labour, forced labour, and unsafe working conditions, which weaken labour relations and sustainable development.
This intervention aims to strengthen Kenya’s capacity to ratify, apply, and report on International Labour Standards (ILS). The ILO will support the government, social partners, and key institutions in aligning national legislation with international norms, addressing legal gaps, and enhancing the enforcement of labour rights, especially for vulnerable groups. The intervention will prioritize the elimination of child labour, forced labour, and trafficking, with targeted capacity-building for labour inspectors, judicial officers, and enforcement agencies.
A central component will be the establishment of an ILS unit within the Ministry of Labour to improve reporting on ratified conventions and strengthen compliance. Gender equality will be a cross-cutting priority, with efforts to promote equal opportunities for women and men and expand women’s participation in capacity-building initiatives.
By supporting national efforts to meet ILO reporting obligations and enhance labour law enforcement, the intervention seeks to foster a fairer and more just labour environment. These efforts will contribute to improved working conditions, protection of labour rights, and inclusive, sustainable economic growth.
